collectible:1.text: Family Crests are some artifacts you can collect throughout Vanaheim in God of War Ragnarök. Here you can learn about how to locate said artifacts during your journey. Here you can find a list of locations to follow so you can acquire these crest's This Family Crest isn't available until you complete The Reckoning main quest.

collectible:2.text: Kvasir's Poems are a unique Easter Egg-type collectible that falls under the Artifacts Set and provides references to many of PlayStation's biggest first-party exclusives. Below you can find details to the exact location of all 14 Kvasir's Poems that can be found scattered about the different Realms and Regions in the game. On this page, all Poems are listed in the order they appear in the Journal.

collectible:3.text: Spirit Mementos are special artifacts you can collect throughout your journey in the game. There are only five Spirit Mementos, things are a little trickier than they first appear. This is because each item is broken up into two pieces, which effectively doubles the amount of work that players have to do. The first part of the Brooch can be found near a large tree to the east of the central area of The Plains.

collectible:4.text: Stolen Treasures are 6 items from other lands  in God of War: Ragnarök  found in Midgard that can be collected and sold. Stolen Treasures are artifacts from other parts of the world that tell of other lands, cultures, and even other gods.

collectible:5.text: Things left behind are artifacts you can collect in the land of the Dwarves, Svartalfheim. You must collect six Artifacts, called Things Left Behind, in Svartalfheim. These items can be identified with a purple light above each object. You can find a few of these artifacts early on in God of War: Ragnarok. For the others, you will need to explore the Realm and complete a specific side quest.

collectible:6.text: The Tributes to Freyr are a set of artefacts found in God of War Ragnarök. Long ago, a Jötunn named Gerð came to Vanaheim, offering to teach the Vanir how to travel between realms using Bifröst light. The Vanir god Freyr always yearned to travel, so he immediately took Gerð up on her offer, exploring the entire World Tree together. Eventually, Gerð had to leave, and Freyr was devastated by her departure.
